Special Advising Note:


All students must do a placement interview before enrolling in their first Mandarin Chinese course at UCSD. Instructions for the interview can be located at the Chinese Studies Program website: http://chinesestudies.ucsd.edu/language/placement-info.html


Chinese Studies is an interdisciplinary program that allows the student interested in China to utilize the university's offerings in various departments to build a major leading to a B.A. degree. The student choosing a major in Chinese Studies must meet the following requirements.

  1. Two years of Mandarin Chinese (CHIN 10 A-B-C and CHIN 20 A-B-C ) or equivalent Chinese knowledge.
  2. Twelve upper-division four-unit courses in Chinese studies topics.

a. Courses must be taken from at least three departments or programs.

b. Three of the twelve courses must be upper-division Chinese history.

c. No more than six of the upper-division courses may be language acquisition courses.

d. A minimum of six upper-division courses must be taken at UCSD.

3. As a rule, all courses must be taken and completed for a letter grade for both the major and minor. Exceptions are granted for CHIN 198 and CHIN 199.


NOTE: One year of Community College course work equals three quarters of UCSD course work.


For more information please visit https://chinesestudies.ucsd.edu/undergraduate/major.html
